about: The run-your-own page, /deploy/, as one Task Object (the AgoraPartners board, November 1, 2026): how to run any slice of ta-amps yourself, the partner compute cards, the security checklist and the probes that check a deployment. Every command follows the owning repository's own instructions; repository addresses are written as GitHub addresses and scripts/build_site.py points each one where its files are served. The partner cards take their state from the facts copied below from the partner compute record of October 31, evidence/sira-are-cascade-2026-10-31/partner_compute_cascade.json in the repository: while a partner's mode is local_verified its card is an offline check, so it shows no numbers and no record line, and each line under 'Checked offline' names the copied fact that keeps it true.
title: Run your own | ta-amps
description: How to run any slice of ta-amps yourself: seed packs in your own agent, Teleion Fabric and Teleion Fabric's model shim on Cloudflare, the Docker sandbox, fine-tuning Muse Glimmer 30B, and the partner compute cards for Modal, Baseten and Fireworks.
heading: Run any slice yourself
lead: You don’t have to adopt the whole stack at once. Start with seed packs, ready-made sets of Tasks, inside an agent you already use, run your own Teleion Fabric and its model shim on Cloudflare, try the whole loop offline in Docker, or fine-tune {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} adapters on your own GPUs.

copy_labels.status_selected: Commands selected. Press Ctrl+C or Command+C to copy.

slices.heading: 1. Choose only the slice you need
slices.lead: Every part speaks plain HTTP JSON and JSON-RPC 2.0 MCP, so each one can run on Cloudflare, in a Linux container or on your own machine without changing an agent’s prompts.

items.title: Slice A: seed packs only, inside the agent you use
items.summary: Take any seed pack’s Task Objects, Task templates and standard-library Python checks straight into the coding agent you already use.
items.when: Best when you want reusable schemas, deterministic checks or nonprofit agent kits without hosting anything.
items.commands:
# Clone the seed-pack library (its address is on Agora's Library page), then, in the clone:
python3 scripts/validate_packs.py
# Run one pack's own checks (standard-library Python, no keys):
make -C packs/frame-by-frame-video-qa/code check

items.title: Slice B: your own Teleion Fabric and its model shim on Cloudflare
items.summary: Run your own queue and Task Object store (Teleion Fabric) and your own shim (Teleion Fabric's model shim) on Cloudflare, with the commands each repository gives.
items.when: Best for teams, labs or nonprofits that want an always-on HTTPS and MCP endpoint, where only one worker holds a Task at a time and no write overwrites a newer one.
items.commands:
# 1. Sign in to your Cloudflare account
npx wrangler login

# Your account needs its own D1 databases: create each one that deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc names
# (npx wrangler d1 create <name>) and put its id in that file before you deploy.

# 2. Teleion Fabric: the queue, the Task Object stores and the /mcp endpoint
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/teleion-fabric-infrastructure-work-and-storage-engine.git
cd tessera-infrastructure-work-and-storage-engine
npx --yes wrangler@4.154.0 secret put BOOTSTRAP_SECRET --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc
npx --yes wrangler@4.154.0 deploy --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc

# 3. Teleion Fabric's model shim: the shim, with its own D1 database
cd ..
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/herma-infrastructure-shim-for-intelligent-agents.git
cd herma-infrastructure-shim-for-intelligent-agents
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 d1 execute ta-amps-herma --remote --file deploy/cloudflare/d1-herma.sql --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc -y
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 deploy --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 secret put BOOTSTRAP_SECRET --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc

items.title: Slice C: the whole loop offline, in Docker
items.summary: Run Teleion Fabric locally, check the starter seed pack, and run a two-worker test of claiming a Task and an independent review, with no keys and no outside network.
items.when: Best for offline demos, internal CI or strict data residency.
items.commands:
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/teleionlabs-teleion-fabric.git
cd teleionlabs-teleion-fabric
docker compose up --build --abort-on-container-exit --exit-code-from sample-worker-smoke

items.title: Slice D: fine-tune {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}, Meta’s open-weight model
items.summary: Start from the QLoRA adapter settings ta-amps used to fine-tune {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} on two free Kaggle T4 GPUs, and the Python packages a GPU worker needs.
items.when: Best when you want to tune your own adapters from your own recorded, reviewed task results.
items.commands:
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/teleionlabs-teleion-fabric.git
cd teleionlabs-teleion-fabric
# The adapter settings ta-amps used for {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}}:
cat training/adapters/glimmer-30b-qlora/adapter_config.json
# The packages a GPU worker needs (install them only inside a GPU worker):
pip install -r training/requirements-train.txt

partners.heading: 2. The same tasks, on partner compute
partners.lead: A task doesn’t care where it runs. These cards say what each partner would do in the system and what has actually run there. Each card’s state comes from the partner compute record.

local_verified.text: Nothing has run on {name}. The code and its rules are checked on our own machine.

live_probe.text: {count} ran on {name}: {when}. Nothing else has run there on record; the code and its rules are also checked on our own machine.

partners.try_title: Try it with your own {name} account
partners.try_prefix: # In a clone of the seed-pack library (its address is on Agora's Library page):

never.heading: What these cards never show
never.text: A cost, speed or training result that no live run measured, a partner’s logo, or a credit amount.

cards.name: Modal
cards.role: Runs a seed pack’s tests again in an isolated sandbox, and fine-tunes {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} with QLoRA.

checked.text: The QLoRA settings for {{model:muse-glimmer-30b}} fit the chosen GPU’s memory.
The isolated sandbox’s contract checks out, with no violations.

cards.name: Baseten
cards.role: Runs many workers at once, paced to stay under the account’s tokens-per-minute limit.

checked.text: The pacing kept a test burst under the tokens-per-minute limit.
Requests that were retried stay in the ledger.

cards.name: Fireworks AI
cards.role: Routes a task to a small specialist adapter behind Teleion Fabric's model shim, with a different adapter as the checker.

checked.text: The routing rule picked an adapter within the shim’s time budget.
A worker checking its own output is blocked.
Personal data in an answer is escalated, not passed on.

record.about: Copied from the partner live-verification record (notes/coordination-2026-10-31/artifacts), read without key values. Each card says what ran, never which accounts exist. A run is a probe whose mode is live_api (or another live mode that is not only ready); its time is the record's verification time. The record keeps its latest probe only, so earlier runs stay listed here as they were read. The deploy build stops when these facts differ from the record's current values.

surfaces.heading: 3. Run the two public sites, Agora and Eranos
surfaces.lead: The sites hold no admin keys. You can host Agora on any static host, and Eranos on its own Cloudflare Worker.

items.title: Agora, the static overview
items.detail: Agora is built from the JSON in site/content/ by standard-library Python, with no npm at run time. Serve the site/ folder from Cloudflare Pages, Workers static assets or any web server.
items.commands:
# Agora's source: https://github.com/ta-amps/agora-public-overview-architecture-setup-and-contribution
# In its folder, check that every page is built from its source:
python3 scripts/build_site.py --check

# Option 1: deploy the site/ folder to Cloudflare Pages
npx wrangler pages deploy site --project-name=agora-hub

# Option 2: serve it with Docker on port 8080
docker build -t ta-amps-agora . && docker run --rm -p 8080:8080 ta-amps-agora

items.title: Eranos, the marketplace (a Cloudflare Worker with D1 and a scoped Teleion Fabric key)
items.detail: Eranos reads and writes Teleion Fabric with a scoped surface key, so visitors can browse reviewed kits and follow requests without touching any admin store.
items.commands:
git clone https://github.com/ta-amps/eranos-public-marketplace-for-public-good-token-burn.git
cd eranos-public-marketplace-for-public-good-token-burn
make check

# The surface key for your own Teleion Fabric (never an admin key):
npx wrangler secret put TESSERA_SURFACE_KEY --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc
pnpm --dir web install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm --dir web build
npx --yes wrangler@4.149.0 deploy --config deploy/cloudflare/wrangler.jsonc

security.heading: 4. A security checklist for your own copy
security.lead: Keep these four boundaries whenever you run your own copy, on Cloudflare or in containers.

items.name: Surface keys and worker keys
items.text: Give web surfaces a read and submit surface key, and give each worker a narrow key scoped to its queues. Never put an admin key in a browser or in a surface’s code.

items.name: Compare-and-set writes
items.text: Create a new Task Object with expected_version 0 and update one with its exact version, so concurrent workers get HTTP 409 Conflict instead of overwriting each other.

items.name: Short-lived sessions for public demos
items.text: When signed-out visitors try live flows, such as the Live Studio, give them a short-lived anonymous session in its own namespace, with a per-address rate limit.

items.name: Probes after every deploy
items.text: Check /v1/health, JSON-RPC tools/list on /mcp and a surface readback before sending traffic or workers to a new deployment.

verify.heading: 5. Check a live deployment
verify.text: Point these three probes at the public ta-amps services, or swap the addresses for your own.
verify.commands:
# 1. Teleion Fabric's health
curl -fsS https://fabric.teleionlabs.com/v1/health

# 2. the model shim's preview of the context it would add (it stores nothing)
curl -fsS -X POST https://shim.teleionlabs.com/api/preview \
  -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"prompt":"How do Tasks and Task Objects work with Agent Harness Feeds?"}'

# 3. The brief agents start from
curl -fsS https://home.ta-amps.workers.dev/llms.txt | head -n 25
